summary.text: One of the fair-cheeked Graeae whom Hesiod names beside Pemphredo as a grey-haired daughter of Phorcys and Ceto; Apollodorus counts her among the three grey sisters who share one eye and one tooth.

story.text: Hesiod names saffron-robed Enyo with Pemphredo among the Graiae grey from their birth, daughters of Phorcys and Ceto and sisters of the Gorgons. Apollodorus makes Enyo one of the three Phorcides — Enyo, Pephredo and Dino — who pass a single eye and tooth among them until Perseus snatches both. Hyginus lists Enyo between Pemphredo and Persis (whom others call Dino). Enyo is the one sister named in all three rolls.
This Enyo is not the war-goddess Enyo, who belongs to a different divine stock.
